title: SRT source
description: Where to receive SRT from, and how much delay to trade for reliability.

mode.title: Connection mode
mode.description: listener waits for a sender to dial in, which is what a phone or a hardware encoder usually wants. caller dials out to a sender that is already waiting. rendezvous is both ends dialling at once, for when a firewall sits between them.

host.title: Address
host.description: In listener mode, the interface to wait on: 0.0.0.0 is every one. In caller mode, the address of the sender.

port.title: Port
port.description: The UDP port. SRT is UDP, so a firewall rule for TCP will not do.

uri.title: Full address
uri.description: An srt:// address pasted from a hardware encoder or another mixer, options and all. When this is set it wins, and host and port are ignored. Anything already in its query string is left alone.

latency_ms.title: Latency budget
latency_ms.description: How long SRT may spend asking for lost packets again before it gives up and passes a gap through. More is steadier on a bad link and adds exactly this much delay. 125 ms is fine on a LAN; 200 to 500 ms suits the public internet.

passphrase.title: Passphrase
passphrase.description: Encrypts the stream. Both ends must use the same one. SRT requires 10 to 79 characters; leave it empty for no encryption.

stream_id.title: Stream id
stream_id.description: The name the sender publishes under, when the far end sorts streams by it. Leave empty when there is only one stream on the port.

auto_reconnect.title: Reconnect on its own
auto_reconnect.description: Dial again when the link drops, rather than waiting for the supervisor to rebuild the source.
